$comment: Duplication that is deliberate. Every entry needs a real reason (enforced). Prefer explicit file pairs over broad globs — this is documentation of a decision, not a suppression bucket. See .agents/skills/duplication/SKILL.md

intentionalPairs.reason: pairql pair versioning: v1 tests are frozen against the old contract on purpose, so the v2 copies must be able to drift independently
pairql pair versioning, same rationale as the CheckIn v1/v2 resolver tests above
reset fixtures are parallel-by-design: each seeded account is meant to be read top-to-bottom in isolation

duet relation accessors (`func child(in db:)`, `func device(in db:)`) are formulaic per-model boilerplate — each is typed to a different model, so collapsing them would need generics that read worse than the repetition

identical test text exercising different production types: each suite's own `testMigrator` resolves to AppMigrator vs FilterMigrator, so the shared body is not shared behavior. sharing it would need generics over the migrator. NB the two deliberately differ on the storage-key assertion — Filter pins the literal "persistent.state.v2" so a key rename fails the test

separate swift packages for separate apps (iosapp lib-ios vs macapp App). the shared `init` is a local test DSL for building flow fixtures; coupling two apps' test suites to share it is a worse trade than the duplication
separate packages with no shared dependency, and the copies are not equivalent: api decodes with the suite's configured `decoder`, macapp with a fresh `JSONDecoder()`
claim vs claim-data resolvers for the same flow: the repeated seed-and-claim setup is what makes each scenario readable on its own
same claim/claim-data pairing as the music resolvers, for apple music
the same claim-data preconditions asserted per app (apple music, blocker); parallel by product shape, not copied
the same empty-account precondition asserted against two different resolvers — similar by nature of the scenario, not copied
distinct onboarding scenarios that necessarily share TestStore setup; the setup is the context that makes each step's failure interpretable
